title: Preface
summary: The partial document covers the annual review of the Caldstone Quarry Heritage Trust for the year 2025. It includes sections on the trust and its mission, financial outlook, archive and collections, membership benefits, site interpretation, and governance.

title: Trust and Mission
summary:
The main points covered in the partial document are:
- The trust's founding in 1987 with the aim of preserving the Caldstone limestone quarry and its industrial heritage.
- The quarry closed in 1962 and became a tourist site in 1991.
- By the end of 2025, the trust had 2,300 members.
- The trust's mission includes the conservation of the quarry landscape, the kiln complex, and the archive of the former quarry company.

nodes.title: Financial Outlook
nodes.summary: The partial document discusses the financial outlook of a trust, focusing on its volunteer training program. It mentions that in 2025, the training was funded from a designated reserve rather than the general budget. Additionally, it details that 84 volunteers completed an accredited course in archive handling and guided tour practice, with 61 of them qualifying as site guides for the 2026 season.

nodes.title: Archive and Collections
nodes.summary: The partial document covers the archive and collections, including 12,400 photographic negatives of quarry operations from 1904 to 1961 and 480 oral history recordings of former quarry workers and their families. It also mentions that in 2025, 2,150 negatives were digitized and 66 oral histories were transcribed. Additionally, a reading room with twelve seats was opened in the old weighbridge office.

nodes.title: Membership Benefits
nodes.summary: The partial document describes the restoration of a kiln complex, funded primarily by membership funds and external grants, with membership fees covering a smaller portion of the cost. The restoration, completed in June 2025, involved the three draw kilns and had a total cost of 214,000 GBP, with 130,000 GBP coming from an industrial heritage grant. Scaffolding was used to protect the original brick linings during the works.

nodes.title: Site Interpretation
nodes.summary: The partial document covers a site interpretation trail around a quarry floor and kiln bank, which is 2.6 kilometers long and includes 18 interpretation panels about the stone extraction process. It also mentions the launch of a new audio guide in three languages in May 2025, which has increased the average visitor dwell time from 48 to 71 minutes.

nodes.title: Governance
nodes.summary: The main points covered in the partial document are the governance structure of a trust, including the board of nine trustees that meets quarterly and the annual members assembly held in October. In 2025, the assembly approved an expansion of the trust's objectives to include adjacent lime woodland and elected two new trustees.
